As a dedicated professional currently serving as a Success Coach/Case Manager at Hispanic Unity of Florida, I
have developed extensive experience supporting youth and families through holistic, strength-based case
management, academic advocacy, and community engagement. My professional background in child welfare,
foster care, youth services, and behavioral health, combined with my academic studies in psychology, child
and adolescent development, and behavioral neuropsychology, has allowed me to build meaningful
relationships with youth while helping families navigate personal, emotional, educational, and social
challenges. Through my studies at Massachusetts College of Liberal Arts and Florida International University,
I developed a strong understanding of child and adolescent development, behavioral psychology, trauma-
informed care, emotional regulation, family systems, and the environmental and neurological factors that
impact youth behavior and long-term development. My continued studies and interests in behavioral
neuropsychology have further strengthened my understanding of cognitive and emotional development in
children and adolescents, particularly how trauma, instability, mental health, and environmental stressors
influence behavior, learning, emotional wellness, and family functioning. These studies have equipped me with
the ability to approach youth and families with empathy, patience, cultural awareness, and evidence-based
understanding. In my current role as a Success Coach, I manage a caseload of youth and families utilizing a
holistic Strength-Based Case Management approach focused on academic achievement, family stability,
emotional wellness, and youth empowerment. I conduct assessments, develop individualized service plans and
goals, coordinate referrals to community resources, and facilitate educational workshops centered around life
skills, civic engagement, academic success, and personal growth. Through this work, I have strengthened my
ability to motivate students, advocate for families, build trust with youth, and support long-term positive
outcomes within underserved communities. My professional background in child welfare and foster care has
further strengthened my passion for advocacy and family support. As a Kinship Licensing Specialist
at ChildNet, I worked directly with children, relative caregivers, and foster families within the dependency and
foster care system. In this role, I conducted comprehensive home studies, assessed family dynamics and safety
concerns, coordinated supportive services, and advocated for safe, stable, and nurturing placements for
children involved in the child welfare system. I also maintained detailed confidential documentation,
collaborated with multidisciplinary teams, and supported families navigating trauma, reunification, placement
stability, and permanency planning. This experience significantly deepened my understanding of childhood
trauma, attachment, crisis intervention, and the importance of supportive and consistent caregiving in child and
adolescent development. Additionally, one of the experiences that has most profoundly shaped my passion for
youth advocacy and community engagement is being an alumna of AMIGOS de las Américas. Through
AMIGOS, I participated in leadership development, cultural immersion, community service, and youth
empowerment initiatives that reinforced my commitment to advocacy, mentorship, and creating meaningful
change within underserved communities. This experience strengthened my leadership, communication,
adaptability, and cultural competency skills while deepening my passion for empowering young people to
recognize their strengths, resilience, and potential. Alongside my professional and academic background, I am
bilingual in English and Spanish and hold CPR, CPI, FARS, CFARS, and WELLES certifications. I am also a
licensed notary public. My experience mentoring and supporting students from elementary through high
school, combined with my background in child welfare, foster care, adolescent behavioral development, and
neuropsychology, allows me to connect with youth and families in a compassionate, supportive, and impactful
manner. I am deeply passionate about continuing to support youth and families through advocacy, mentorship,
behavioral support, and community-based services, and I look forward to the opportunity to continue making a
meaningful impact through my work.
Sincerely,
Nalisha S. De Castro

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Program Operations Manager position with Adolescent Behavioral Health. With a background in forensic psychology and healthcare operations, combined with several years of experience leading teams, developing workflows, and supporting patients and healthcare partners, I am excited by the opportunity to bring my leadership and operational experience to an organization focused on improving the lives of adolescents and their families.

In my current role within a healthcare organization specializing in Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) and Chronic Care Management (CCM), I lead a team of 13 employees supporting patients, healthcare providers, and clinical partners. I oversee day-to-day operations, quality and performance, escalations, process improvement, staff coaching, and the development of workflows and standard operating procedures. This experience has taught me how to thrive in fast-paced environments, identify operational gaps, build practical solutions, and lead teams through change.

My academic background in forensic psychology has given me a strong foundation in behavioral science, human development, and the factors that influence behavior and decision-making. I am particularly drawn to adolescent behavioral health because of the opportunity to combine that academic foundation with my professional experience in healthcare, leadership, and operations. While I am not a clinician, I understand the importance of creating an environment where clinical teams can do their work effectively and where patients and families feel supported, respected, and cared for.

As a leader, I take a hands-on and collaborative approach. I believe in setting clear expectations, supporting employees with the resources and coaching they need to succeed, and holding people accountable while recognizing their strengths and contributions. I also enjoy building structure in evolving environments and continuously looking for ways to improve workflows, communication, and the overall experience for both staff and the individuals we serve.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare leadership experience, operational mindset, and background in forensic psychology to your team. I am particularly excited about the possibility of contributing to a growing behavioral-health program where strong operations and compassionate leadership can directly support better outcomes for adolescents and their families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and perspective could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Mariam Dominguez
